article.title: Afghanistan sees drop in men’s university enrollment as women remain barred
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.

University enrollment among men in Afghanistan in 2026 has fallen nearly one-third from levels before the Taliban’s takeover, while women’s enrollment has remained at zero for the third consecutive year.

A new U.N. report says enrollment at public and private universities in Afghanistan totaled approximately 208,000 students, all men, in 2026, down from about 430,000 students, including 124,000 women, in 2020.

“Women remain excluded from formal participation, male enrollment is substantially lower than in 2019, the academic workforce has shrunk, and private institutions face continuing financial pressure,” the report said.
The Taliban barred women from university education in December 2022 and from medical training institutes, which offer diplomas in nursing, midwifery and other health fields December 2024.
Since seizing power in 2021, the Taliban have placed sweeping restrictions on women’s rights and freedom.

Under the Taliban, women and girls are not allowed to get an education beyond 6th grade. They are barred from working with government and non-government organizations, going to parks, gyms, public baths, and beauty salons.
The group has issued more than 100 decrees that curb women’s and girls’ rights and freedoms, including their right to get an education.

Meanwhile, the Taliban have tightened their control over men’s higher education by imposing numerous restrictions, such as conducting new oral exams on religious topics, dress codes, removing hundreds of books and other learning materials, and discontinuing over a dozen subjects related to human rights, democracy, gender, governance and other social science fields, according to the U.N.
Farid, a university student in Kabul, told VOA that students have few incentives to pursue higher education.
“There are only a few opportunities for graduates. This makes people not be motivated to continue their studies,” said Farid, who did not want his full name disclosed for security reasons.
He added that most of the students also face financial problems, forcing them to discontinue their studies.
“The economic situation has worsened. Students are not even able to pay for commuting to the university daily,” he said.
Farid added that students are also worried about their job prospects after graduation.
Mohammad Asif Nang, former deputy minister for education in Afghanistan, told VOA that the future of higher education in Afghanistan is uncertain.
“For example, a young man loses hope of a better future when he cannot find himself in a system based on competition, merit and professional qualifications,” he said.
“These trends affect not only higher education itself but also the future supply of qualified professionals across Afghanistan’s education, health and wider service sector,” the U.N. report said.
zh: 阿富汗男性大學入學率下降，而女性仍被禁止就學
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）達里語原文報導。
2026年，阿富汗男性的大學入學率較塔利班接管前下降了近三分之一，而女性的入學率則連續第三年維持在零。
一份新的聯合國報告指出，2026年阿富汗公立及私立大學的總註冊人數約為208,000名學生，全為男性；相較之下，2020年的總註冊人數約為430,000名學生，其中包含124,000名女性。
報告指出：「女性仍被排除在正式參與之外，男性註冊人數較2019年大幅減少，學術人員規模已縮減，而私立院校則持續面臨財務壓力。」
塔利班於2022年12月禁止女性接受大學教育，並於2024年12月禁止女性進入提供護理、助產及其他醫療領域文憑的醫療培訓機構就讀。
自2021年掌權以來，塔利班對婦女的權利與自由施加了全面性的限制。
在塔利班統治下，婦女和女童不得接受小學六年級以上的教育。她們被禁止在政府及非政府組織工作，也不得前往公園、健身房、公共澡堂及美容院。
該組織已頒布超過100項法令，限制婦女和女童的權利與自由，包括她們接受教育的權利。
與此同時，據聯合國表示，塔利班透過實施多項限制措施，進一步加強了對男性高等教育的控制，例如針對宗教主題舉行新的口試、實施服裝規定、撤下數百本圖書及其他學習資料，並停開十餘門與人權、民主、性別、治理及其他社會科學領域相關的課程。
喀布爾的大學生法里德向美國之音表示，學生們幾乎沒有動力去追求高等教育。
「畢業生的就業機會寥寥無幾。這讓人們缺乏繼續深造的動力，」法里德表示。他基於安全考量，不願透露全名。
他補充說，大多數學生也面臨經濟困難，迫使他們不得不輟學。
「經濟狀況已惡化。學生連每天往返大學的交通費都負擔不起，」他說道。
法里德補充說，學生們也擔心畢業後的就業前景。
阿富汗前教育部副部長穆罕默德·阿西夫·南格向美國之音表示，阿富汗高等教育的未來前景不明朗。
「舉例來說，當一名年輕人無法在以競爭、績效和專業資格為基礎的體制中找到自己的定位時，他便會對更美好的未來失去希望，」他說道。
聯合國報告指出：「這些趨勢不僅影響高等教育本身，也將影響阿富汗教育、衛生及更廣泛服務部門未來合格專業人才的供應。」
